title: whole first, then chosen
subtitle: on outgrowing the need, and learning what it means to pick someone on purpose
author: NASIRR "G" MAYO

body.text: on outgrowing the need, and learning what it means to pick someone on purpose
i caught an uber home by myself last night.

i'd planned the date with intention. i had work in the morning, so i wanted the night to be cool and regular, nothing extra. we showed up together. i left alone. and somewhere between the door and the ride home, i realized none of the intention i put into that night had been seen.
that hurt. i'm not gonna pretend it didn't.

but sitting in that backseat, i noticed something else under the pain. a younger version of me would've taken that night as proof i was missing something. that i needed someone to fix it. this version of me just felt it, named it, and kept riding.
that's the shift i've been trying to understand.
the need was never about her
when i was younger, i approached relationships from a place of need. a woman had to BE in my life for a reason, and the reason usually wasn't her. it was what she could fill.

looking back, a lot of what i called need was really a wound. i was looking outside myself to settle something inside myself. and because i believed a woman was supposed to do that, i tried to fit women into boxes they were never built for.
that wasn't fair to them. it wasn't healthy for me either.
some things aren't another person's job to fix. there are parts of us we have to confront on our own, and no partner, no matter how good, can do that work for us.
what changes when you can stand on your own

when you believe you need someone, you'll tolerate things you shouldn't. you'll overlook what doesn't fit. you'll hold on longer than you should, because losing them feels like losing a piece of yourself.
when you know you can stand on your own, the questions change.
do i actually enjoy this person? do our values line up? do i feel appreciated? do i like who i am around them? and the big one:
if i can live a full life without you, what makes me want to share it with you?
i don't think that question makes love smaller. i think it makes it honest. choosing someone you don't depend on to repair you is a more intentional kind of choice.

but i have to be careful here too. being whole doesn't mean needing nothing. i still need care, consistency, communication, affection, accountability, effort. i can be complete on my own and still need my partner to show up. those aren't contradictions.
the difference is i'm not asking anyone to be the missing piece anymore.
the door i keep walking back to
there's a woman i once thought i needed. back then, i couldn't imagine life without her. time proved me wrong. we both grew, lived other things, and life kept moving.
what's strange is the need faded, but the want didn't. it grew.

so now i'm asking myself something i don't have the answer to yet: is the woman i once needed the same woman i should want now? or am i walking back to a familiar door because i remember what it meant at another point in my life?

history matters. but history alone doesn't make two people compatible today. and wanting someone isn't automatically a reason to pursue them. the want has to be backed by reciprocity, respect, and a real willingness to build.

maybe the honest question isn't whether i still need her. maybe it's whether we can meet each other as the people we are now, without expecting the relationship to play the roles we gave it when we were younger.
widening the room

i've caught myself thinking in percentages lately, like there's a 25% of women who might be right for me and a 75% who aren't. i'm not proud of how that sounds, but i think it's telling me something real, just not about women. it's telling me about my environment.

if the right people are hard to find where i am, maybe the answer is to stop looking in the same places. i haven't really traveled yet. maybe i need to go see outside, meet people who challenge what i think a relationship can look like.
or maybe i need to sit alone for a while first and get clear on what i'm actually looking for.
i want to be discerning without being closed off. i don't want my standards to turn into a formula that keeps me from recognizing a good person who doesn't fit the picture.
where i'm landing, for now

here's what i want: to want my partner first, and then grow into needing her. not a need born from emptiness. the kind that comes from trust, shared experience, and choosing each other again + again, not because we can't survive apart, but because we value what we're building.
i'm not there yet. so this week, i'm doing the thing that actually gets me closer.

seven days, monday to sunday. all of it goes into me + my projects. not as a punishment, and not as a wall. as practice. because if i want to be chosen by someone who's whole, i have to keep becoming someone who's whole too.
it's ME week.
and maybe that uber ride home was the lesson i didn't know i needed.
